problem:
The $6$th root of unity ${e}^{4\pi \text{i}/3}$ can be written as 

$$
{e}^{4\pi \text{i}/3}={z}^{p},
$$

where $z$ is the principal $6$th root of unity. What is the value of $p?$

The $4$th root of unity ${e}^{3\pi \text{i}/2}$ can be written as 

$$
{e}^{3\pi \text{i}/2}={z}^{p},
$$

where $z$ is the principal $4$th root of unity. What is the value of $p?$

$p=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the $4$th roots of unity can be written in the form

$$
{e}^{2k\pi \text{i}/4}
$$

where $k=0,1,2,3.$ 

We obtain the *principal* $4$th root of unity by substituting $k=1:$

$$
z={e}^{2\cdot 1\cdot \pi \text{i}/4}={e}^{\pi \text{i}/2}
$$

We can write the given root of unity as a power of the principal root as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{3\pi \text{i}/2} & =({e}^{\pi \text{i}/2})^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=3.$
